speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit. The loaf goes against the notch before anyone cuts it. I will not have a short loaf pretended into a full one by a hungry man.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It is short by a finger, Mistress. Same as yesterday. The penny is on the board beside it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny, then, and short by a finger. I am not here to argue the baker into a better week.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence for the meal, Master Shakespeare. And the sixpence for firing and washing. It is the week's, and I will have it once, not once at dinner and once at the stair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once. Sixpence. There it is. Candles are mine, and I am not burning the house's to save them.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib came off the book when he heard the plate. He is under the bench now. He will be on the book again before grace is done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let him. The page can spare him for as long as a meal takes, and not longer.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Your Sunday letter is still on the table in your chamber, folded, and not sealed for a Monday. Thursday's carrier has it. I am not sending Alse to Carter Lane with it tomorrow to save you a wait.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thursday. It stays folded. I am not opening it to improve it. It said what it said on Septuagesima, and the day of coming is still not in it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Septuagesima is a long word for a letter. Does the carrier charge more for a long word?

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: He charges twopence for a letter, Alse, and sixpence for a parcel, and nothing at all for your questions. Eat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twopence on Thursday, when he has it in his hand. Not today. Today is threepence and the sixpence, and that is the whole of my purse at this table.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Master Verbeke has the end of the bench. He nodded at the loaf and said nothing. Is that manners, in Flanders?

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It is manners at my table, wherever a man learned them. You will not ask him to perform his country between the bread and the salt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No. He lodges here. He is not a story for a Sunday. The loom in Norton Folgate can wait until Monday without our help.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And the play can wait until you have eaten. I have had the plot of the forsworn gentlemen. I am not taking it again with the gravy. Four young men swear off women and keep it till dinner. I believed that the first time.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we will not have it a second time. The yard has heard it. Your kitchen has heard it. The letter has four lines of it, and those four lines can stand until Thursday.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I have not seen it. I have heard the floor. The floor is not the same as a yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The floor is what you have, Alse, until someone takes you. Today is not that day. Eat the short loaf and call it a full Sunday.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mark me. After dinner I count the spoons. I count them because I count them, not because I have a name ready. You will still be in the house. Callers have been up your stair all month.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Count them. If one is short, I had rather hear it in the kitchen than in a story told at the door. I am not going out.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will wash them first. A dirty spoon counts as badly as a missing one, and worse, because it comes back to the board.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Wash them, then. And leave Gib off the clean board. A cat is not a sixth guest, whatever he thinks when he hears a plate.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Five of us at the most, and the cat under the bench. I have paid. I am going up until you call the count. The letter stays where it is.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Up, then. When I am wrong about a spoon I will say so. When I am right you will hear it from the stair. I do not whisper a shortage.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will call you if the count is short, sir. I would rather find a spoon than listen to one being discussed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Find it, if it is there to find. I will be in the chamber, and I will not be rewriting Sunday's page.
